volumes.title: The Bondage and the Liberation

volumes.reader_summary: A river, a basket, and a fugitive begin a liberation that will outgrow all three. volumes.title: The Land and the Crowns
volumes.historical_turn: Settlement and conquest claims → judges → monarchy → dynastic state + temple
volumes.institutional_struggle: Local survival, conquest ideology, kingship, prophetic challenge, and sacred construction compete for legitimacy
volumes.intimate_change: Ruth secures belonging; Saul, David, and Solomon gain authority that exposes and enlarges their failures
volumes.cosmological_discovery: Victory cannot prove divine approval; an office and its occupant remain distinguishable
volumes.entry_state: A new generation faces inhabited land while carrying contested promises and wilderness law
volumes.exit_state: A splendid central kingdom conceals conscription, unpaid debts, dynastic violence, and an approaching fracture
volumes.reader_summary: The land is already inhabited. Conquest accounts, local memories, marriage bargains, and rescue stories collide before the demand for a king turns them into a national story. Ruth seeks a future in the margins. Saul and David discover what a crown can license; Solomon builds a magnificent answer to questions he cannot settle.

volumes.title: The Kingdoms and the Exile
